A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Privacy Collapse study. The complete main texts and appendices are readable, and retained experiments, equations, figures and tables can be matched across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning experiments on contextual privacy, safety and capabilities, alongside backdoor experiments and mechanistic analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds mitigation experiments, failure categorization and a human-annotation reliability study.

M1.justification: Section 5.4 extends the diagnostic study into mitigation: training samples are ranked using the existing projection method, the bottom 10% are removed, and models are retrained. It also introduces helpful/control data mixing as a training intervention. v1 suggested filtering as future work but did not implement these mitigation procedures.

E1.justification: Training corpora, benchmark coverage and task domains are retained. The additions filter or mix existing training data, categorize existing privacy failures and review samples from the existing CIMemories evaluation.

E2.justification: Corresponding original experiments retain the same models and comparison conditions. The new mitigation tests reuse unfiltered or pure-helpful training as references; filtering and mixing are the new interventions being evaluated.

E3.justification: Added experiments specify bottom-10% filtering, helpful-data proportions of 100%, 90%, 75% and 50%, and two independent annotators evaluating 30 randomly selected responses. Existing benchmark sample sizes, training epochs and evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds mitigation testing and mixture sensitivity analysis in Section 5.4 and Appendix I, a contextual-integrity failure breakdown in Appendix H.2, and human evaluation in Appendix J. These substantially extend the diagnostic evidence. The in-context learning analysis is retained from v1 Appendix C and moved to Section 5.5.

E5.justification: Appendix J introduces inter-annotator reliability reporting through percentage agreement and Cohen's kappa. Both versions already report three independently seeded fine-tuning runs and error bars; no increased run count or revised uncertainty-estimation practice is stated.

E6.justification: Original reported results are retained, while v2 adds absolute accuracies, failure proportions, mitigation outcomes and annotation agreement. Table I.1 reports privacy drops changing from -24.3% to -14.9% and -20.4% to -11.1% under filtering; Table I.2 reports -65.0% for 50% helpful-data mixing versus -98.1% for pure helpful data. Appendix J adds 93.3% inter-annotator agreement and kappa 0.71.

T1.justification: Section 3 adds an explicit threat model, a binary leakage-event definition and two inequalities defining privacy collapse through increased expected leakage and bounded change in aggregate safety/capability performance. The existing projection mathematics is retained; no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction's contribution statements are unchanged. The conclusion retains the claims that benign fine-tuning can selectively degrade contextual privacy, that diverse training characteristics induce this failure, and that conventional evaluations can miss it.

C2.justification: v2 interprets filtering and mixing as rebalancing learned information-access norms and interprets the failure breakdown as inappropriate information flow rather than recipient-role misclassification. It also adds uncertainty about whether unlearning techniques address contextual privacy failures. Earlier mechanistic interpretations remain intact.

D1.justification: The appendix changes from planning a public release of models, synthetic datasets and code to stating that these artifacts are released. The existing code link, hardware description, software, training APIs and original hyperparameter disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Goel et al. (2026), Auditing Language Model Unlearning via Information Decomposition, and briefly distinguishes memorization-oriented mitigation from contextual privacy protection. The broader related-work discussion and novelty positioning are retained.

P1.justification: The revision adds localized subsections and Appendices H-J, moves the existing in-context learning discussion into Section 5.5, updates appendix references and shortens the conclusion. Most existing prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: Four tables are added: H.1-H.2 for absolute accuracy and failure categories, and I.1-I.2 for mitigation results. Existing figures retain their artwork and contents, with several repositioned by text reflow; appendix displays are also renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 provides measured mitigation evidence where v1 only suggested filtering, and adds useful failure categorization and annotation-reliability evidence. These modestly improve practical usefulness and evidential coverage. The gains are limited by unquantified judge-human agreement and the new absolute-accuracy summary in Section 4.1.2, whose stated ranges do not consistently match Table H.1.
